newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian 10-year bond tests new ground on data.
newsitem.headline: Australian 10-year bond tests new ground on data.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract struck a record high of 93.670 after both June and quarterly retail trade data proved weaker than median expectations.
*Costello to give speech around 1.15 p.m. (0315 GMT).

Australian 10-year bond futures struck a record high of 93.670 after both June and quarterly retail trade data proved weaker than median expectations, taking the benchmark yield to its lowest level since the early 1980s.

The market was fairly bullish going into the data in the wake of Wednesday's 1/2 point cut in official rates, which has led some analsyts to expect a further easing, and after a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries.
"The net result is we are now in a position to make an assault on (a yield of) 6.20 percent and get mighty close to parity with the U.S.," said Stephen Roberts at UBS Australia.

"After the rate cut, and the rationale for it, any signs of the data still erring to the weak side, definitely leaves the door ajar for the potential for another rate cut. I don't think it will be there, but from time to time the market will," Roberts added.
June retail trade fell 1.8 percent, compared with a median forecast for a 0.4 percent rise and the most pesimistic expectation for a 1.5 percent fall.
Second quarter real retail trade dropped 0.5 percent against an expected 0.1 percent rise, and means consumption spending will be a fairly soft element in GDP.
Hans Kunnen, chief economist at Colonial State Bank also believes parity is achievable on the 10-year bond yield spread to the U.S.
"The rally can continue providing people believe that government's can continue fiscal restraint and inflation is under control," Kunnen said.

U.S. Treasuries put in a strong rally on Wednesday, helping the initial rally in local debt, amid a broad spread of demand against a backdrop of benign inflation, reduced supply and a strengthening U.S. dollar.

The market outperformed against the dollar bloc, although this was more so at the long end and caused the bond yield curve to give up some of Wednesday's steepening which followed the rate cut to 5.0 percent official rates.
